description: Unsupervised duvet annotation loop state. RFC 7748 pilot complete; queue from rfc-candidates.md gates.

requirements.quote:
When receiving such an array, implementations of X25519
(but not X448) MUST mask the most significant bit in the final byte.

Implementations MUST accept non-canonical values and process them as
if they had been reduced modulo the field prime.

For X25519, the unused, most significant bit MUST be
zero.

The trace of Frobenius MUST NOT be in {0, 1} in order to rule out
the attacks described in [smart], [satoh], and [semaev], as in
[brainpool] and [safecurves].
requirements.skip_reason: Theoretical curve security property of Curve25519. Satisfied by the curve definition, not addressable as a code annotation.

requirements.quote:
MOV Degree [reducing]: the embedding degree MUST be greater than
(order - 1) / 100, as in [brainpool] and [safecurves].
requirements.skip_reason: Theoretical curve security property of Curve25519. Satisfied by the curve definition, not addressable as a code annotation.

requirements.quote:
CM Discriminant: discriminant D MUST be greater than 2^100, as in
[safecurves].
requirements.skip_reason: Theoretical curve security property of Curve25519. Satisfied by the curve definition, not addressable as a code annotation.

requirements.quote:
Within the scope of any encryption key
K, the nonce value MUST be unique.
requirements.skip_reason: Caller obligation, not library behavior. The AEAD/EVP API accepts a caller-supplied nonce; aws-lc cannot enforce uniqueness across calls. No code path implements or checks this.

requirements.quote:
That is, the set of nonce
values used with any given key MUST NOT contain any duplicate
values.
requirements.skip_reason: Caller obligation, not library behavior. The AEAD/EVP API accepts a caller-supplied nonce; aws-lc cannot enforce uniqueness across calls. No code path implements or checks this.

requirements.quote:
The 3-bit field MUST NOT have a value of zero,
which would correspond to a 16-bit integrity check value.

The Reserved bits are reserved for future expansions and MUST be set
to zero.

Bit 6 corresponds to the Adata bit in the B_0 block, but as
this bit is not used here, it is reserved and MUST be set to zero.

If the T value is not correct, the receiver MUST NOT reveal any
information except for the fact that T is incorrect.

The receiver
MUST NOT reveal the decrypted message, the value T, or any other
information.

This is roughly 16 million
terabytes, which should be more than enough for most applications.)
In an environment where this limit might be reached, the sender MUST
ensure that the total number of block cipher encryption operations in
the CBC-MAC and encryption together does not exceed 2^61.

The recipient MUST verify the CBC-MAC before releasing any
information such as the plaintext.

If the CBC-MAC verification
fails, the receiver MUST destroy all information, except for the fact
that the CBC-MAC verification failed.

If unwrapping
produces an unexpected value, then the algorithm implementation MUST
return an error, and it MUST NOT return any key data.
In all cases, the AlgorithmIdentifier parameter field MUST be absent.
requirements.skip_reason: ASN.1/OID encoding requirement, not algorithm behavior. The AlgorithmIdentifier and OID tables live in crypto/obj and crypto/asn1, outside this config's source patterns (crypto/fipsmodule, crypto/evp). Not annotatable in scope.

requirements.quote:
Implementations of such
protocols that make use of SHA-224 MUST use the following object
identifier.
requirements.skip_reason: ASN.1/OID encoding requirement, not algorithm behavior. The AlgorithmIdentifier and OID tables live in crypto/obj and crypto/asn1, outside this config's source patterns (crypto/fipsmodule, crypto/evp). Not annotatable in scope.

requirements.quote: The context (if present at all) MUST be empty.

In particular, unless the underlying
protocol does not require it, the receiver MUST buffer the entire
message (or enough information to reconstruct it, e.g., compressed or
encrypted version) to be verified.

Implementations MUST make sure to use the constants (Nh) and function
calls (LabeledExtract and LabeledExpand) of the appropriate KDF when
implementing DHKEM.

Senders and recipients MUST validate KEM inputs and outputs as
described in Section 7.1.

If
used inside a KEM algorithm, suite_id MUST start with "KEM" and
identify this KEM algorithm; if used in the remainder of HPKE, it
MUST start with "HPKE" and identify the entire ciphersuite in use.

The PSK MUST have at least 32 bytes of entropy and SHOULD be of
length Nh bytes or longer.
requirements.skip_reason: PSK modes not implemented. aws-lc supports HPKE_MODE_BASE and HPKE_MODE_AUTH only; psk and psk_id are always absent (NULL, 0).

The PSK MUST have at least 32 bytes of entropy and SHOULD be of

requirements.quote:
That
is, if a non-default value is provided for one of them, then the

requirements.quote:
Implementations MAY use a
sequence number that is shorter than the nonce length (padding on the
left with zero), but MUST raise an error if the sequence number
overflows.
The sender's context MUST NOT be used for decryption.

Similarly, the
recipient's context MUST NOT be used for encryption.

If ContextS.Seal() or ContextR.Open() would
cause the seq field to overflow, then the implementation MUST fail
with an error.

Future specifications that define new KDFs MUST specify a
bound for L.
requirements.skip_reason: Addressed to specification authors, not implementers. Requires future RFCs to state bounds or support; no code can satisfy it.

requirements.quote:
Future
specifications which define new KEMs MUST indicate whether these

requirements.skip_reason: Addressed to specification authors, not implementers. Requires future RFCs to state bounds or support; no code can satisfy it.

requirements.quote:
Some deserialized public keys MUST be validated before they can be
used.
requirements.skip_reason: Forward reference to Section 7.1.4 with no independent obligation. The concrete X25519 validation it points to is cited separately.

requirements.quote:
If the private key is an integer outside the
range [0, order-1], where order is the order of the curve being used,
the private key MUST be reduced to its representative in [0, order-1]
before being serialized.
requirements.skip_reason: No NIST-curve KEM implemented. The only KEM is DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256); P-256/384/521 code paths do not exist.

requirements.quote:
The
SerializePrivateKey() function MUST clamp its output and the
DeserializePrivateKey() function MUST clamp its input, where
_clamping_ refers to the bitwise operations performed on k in the
decodeScalar25519() and decodeScalar448() functions defined in
Section 5 of [RFC7748].
requirements.skip_reason: aws-lc clamps the X25519 scalar inside the scalar multiplication rather than at serialize/deserialize; X25519_keypair deliberately inverts the masking to detect non-conforming peers. Not cited because the literal serialize/deserialize clamping this requires is not where aws-lc performs it. Worth a maintainer's review.

requirements.quote:
The following public keys are subject to validation if the group
requires public key validation: the sender MUST validate the
recipient's public key pkR; the recipient MUST validate the ephemeral
public key pkE; in authenticated modes, the recipient MUST validate
the sender's static public key pkS.
requirements.skip_reason: No NIST-curve KEM implemented. The only KEM is DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256); P-256/384/521 code paths do not exist.

requirements.quote:
For P-256, P-384, and P-521, senders and recipients MUST perform
partial public key validation on all public key inputs, as defined in
Section 5.6.2.3.4 of [keyagreement].
requirements.skip_reason: No NIST-curve KEM implemented. The only KEM is DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256); P-256/384/521 code paths do not exist.

requirements.quote:
Additionally,
senders and recipients MUST ensure the Diffie-Hellman shared secret
is not the point at infinity.
requirements.skip_reason: No NIST-curve KEM implemented. The only KEM is DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256); P-256/384/521 code paths do not exist.

requirements.quote:
For X25519 and X448, public keys and Diffie-Hellman outputs MUST be
validated as described in [RFC7748].

In particular, recipients MUST
check whether the Diffie-Hellman shared secret is the all-zero value
and abort if so.

Future specifications that define new KEMs MUST
indicate whether or not Auth and AuthPSK modes are supported.
requirements.skip_reason: Addressed to specification authors, not implementers. Requires future RFCs to state bounds or support; no code can satisfy it.

requirements.quote:
An ikm input to DeriveKeyPair() (Section 7.1.3) MUST NOT be reused
elsewhere, in particular not with DeriveKeyPair() of a different KEM.
requirements.skip_reason: Caller obligation. Applies to the application driving the HPKE context (message ordering, loss detection, ikm reuse); the library cannot enforce it across calls.

The randomness used in Encap() and AuthEncap() to generate the KEM

o  Words 13-15 are a nonce, which MUST not be repeated for the same

requirements.quote:
The pair (r,s) should be unique, and
MUST be unpredictable for each invocation (that is why it was

constant, but needs to be modified as follows before being used: ("r"

Any document that specifies the use of Poly1305 as a
MAC algorithm for some protocol MUST specify that 256 bits are
allocated for the integrity key.
requirements.skip_reason: Specification-author actor. Addressed to documents that specify Poly1305 for a protocol, not to an implementation. Same category as the RFC 9180 "future specifications MUST" requirements.

requirements.quote:
This MUST be
unique per invocation with the same key, so it MUST NOT be
randomly generated.
requirements.skip_reason: Caller obligation. Constrains how the caller derives the nonce it passes in; aws-lc neither generates nor sequences the nonce for ChaCha20-Poly1305.

requirements.quote: The Poly1305 key MUST be unpredictable to an attacker.

For this reason, with online protocols,
implementation MUST use a constant-time comparison function rather
than relying on optimized but insecure library functions such as the
C language's memcmp().

Additionally, any protocol using this algorithm MUST include the
complete tag to minimize the opportunity for forgery.
requirements.skip_reason: Upper bound only; a caller may request a truncated tag. Not an aws-lc divergence: the check has been upper-bound-only since Adam Langley's original BoringSSL commit de0b20268 (2014-06-20), which predates RFC 8439, and current upstream BoringSSL (crypto/cipher/e_chacha20poly1305.cc, master) still has the identical check. EVP_AEAD_CTX_init documents truncation as intended for every AEAD: 'Authentication tags may be truncated by passing a size as |tag_len|' (include/openssl/aead.h). Annotated type=TODO so it stays uncited and visible; tightening it would diverge from the documented EVP_AEAD contract.
